market_question: Will US withdraw from NATO before 2027?
reasoning: A formal US withdrawal from NATO is an extreme, politically costly move with major bipartisan opposition and legal hurdles. Trump has focused on burden-sharing, not exit, and even unilateral executive action would face lawsuits and Congressional pushback. A 3% chance seems more realistic than the market's 8.4%, suggesting the market overprices YES.
evidence_points: Trump has repeatedly demanded allies increase defense spending but has never pledged to withdraw the US from NATO.
The FY2024 NDAA includes a provision barring the president from unilaterally withdrawing from NATO without Senate consent or an act of Congress.
Past US treaty withdrawals (like the INF Treaty) required formal notice but none were as strategically foundational as NATO, making denunciation politically explosive.
sources_consulted: FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act, Section 1250
Council on Foreign Relations analysis on US-NATO relations
